ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a slanted straight line extending from the lower left to the upper right, intersecting a steeper straight line extending from the upper left to the lower right. At this upper intersection point, the right side is labeled 100°, and the lower-left side is labeled ∠1. Reasoning: ∠1 and the 100° angle are adjacent at the same intersection point, and their outer sides form a straight line, so they are a pair of supplementary adjacent angles. The sum of supplementary adjacent angles is 180°, therefore ∠1 = 180° - 100° = 80°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two intersecting straight lines at the upper crossing: the rising diagonal from the left vertex to the upper right intersects the steep line running from upper left to lower right. The angle labeled 100° is one of the angles at this intersection, and ∠1 is the adjacent angle sharing a side with the 100° angle. Since adjacent angles forming a straight line are supplementary, compute ∠1 = 180° − 100° = 80°.
